|  |  |

## Reduction installation

The motor is connected via a custom shaft to a gearbox with a **23.04:1** reduction by Faulhaber.[^1] Both parts are held in place by 3D-printed plates. The output shaft of the gearbox has its own bearing on the inside of the gearbox, and is also supported mid-way on the shaft by a 4×8 mm flanged bearing. This leaves **5 mm of shaft length free** for the crank to be mounted on. A flat on the shaft helps lock the rotation of the M3 screw extending through the crank.

[^1]: [Faulhaber gearhead reduction ratios](https://www.faulhaber.com/fileadmin/Import/Media/DE_GEARHEADS_REDUCTION_RATIOS.pdf) (accessed 20.02.2024).

::: {layout-ncol="2"}
![Faulhaber gearbox](/Fig/fhaber.jpg)
:::

First, we need to press + glue our sun gear is already pressed onto the motor shaft from [Module 2](02-motor.qmd).

Next, we need to install the gearbox to the motor and fixing the pair to the plates.

1.  Slide the gearbox onto the motor shaft so the sun gear engages the planets. It should seat with light hand pressure, if it resists, back off and check the sun gear is square on the shaft rather than forcing it.

2.  Fix the blue part of the gearbox: the custom screws that come with the gearbox on one side, and **M2.5×10** screws on the other.

3.  Check the output turns freely by hand through a full revolution before applying power.

4.  Close the gearbox: the **silver part threads onto the blue part**. Don't tighten it.

5.  Attach the **second vertical bracket** to the silver part of the gearbox with **3 × M2.5** screws.

6.  Secure that bracket to the **bottom fuselage plate** with **3 × M2** screws. The motor bracket from [Module 2](02-motor.qmd) is already on the same plate, so between them the two brackets set the alignment of the whole drivetrain. Check the output still turns freely once both are bolted down.

### Sun gear

The sun gear from the Faulhaber 23.04:1 gearbox. Press onto shaft (glue if needed). Check that it fits into the reduction, without touching the first stage. Use the back end of the caliper for this.

## Tail

## Trailing edge holder

The wing root is driven by the gears and sweeps through the full **60°** set in [Module 5](05-frame-crank.qmd). The trailing edge is not driven. It is anchored to the **tail tube**, and that anchor is what makes the membrane twist as the wing sweeps. It sets the angle of attack the wing sees through the stroke. Move it and the wing behaves differently. So this part is a trim adjustment as much as it is a mount, which is why both its positions have to stay changeable after the robot is built.

This part is a design exercise. The requirements are fixed; the mechanism is not.

| Requirement | Why |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Rotates with the wing through the whole stroke | The root swings 34° up and 26° down. An anchor that cannot follow loads the membrane in the one direction it cannot take. |
| Adjustable **longitudinally**, along the tube | Fore/aft position sets wing twist. This is the trim actually reached for in [Module 11](11-wet-testing.qmd). |
| Each Wing mounts can change **laterally and longitudinally** | Sets how far the anchor stands off the boom, and is how left and right are matched. |
| Wing comes off without dismantling anything | Wings get swapped, damaged and rebuilt. Nothing about this joint may be permanent. |
| Survives repeated wet cycling | To not fail at competition |

: What the trailing edge holder has to do {#tbl-te-requirements}

### Find a solution

Both flexible and rigid solutions are possible. For a rigid solution, the mount half is straightforward: a **split collar** that slides along the tail tube and clamps with an M2 screw into a square half nut, per the house convention in [Design notes](/reference/design-notes.qmd). Sliding it gives the longitudinal adjustment, rotating it about the tube gives some of the lateral, and a slotted arm gives the rest.

The design must be justified against @tbl-te-requirements, and the choices defended.

### Attach the wing

Connect each wing's trailing edge to its holder.

::: callout-warning
## Both sides must be set identically

Different longitudinal stations left and right means different twist left and right, which is a roll bias -the same failure mode as mismatched wings in [Module 7](07-wings.qmd).
:::

::: callout-note
